speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what percentage of Singapore's carbon emissions is currently contributed by air-conditioning, vehicle transport and waste incineration; and (b) how can Singapore become more efficient in these activities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what is the carbon footprint generated by the waste incineration process in Singapore; and (b) whether measures, such as carbon capture and sequestration or carbonation of bottom ash, are in place or being considered to reduce this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Singapore is fully committed to reducing our emissions under our Paris Agreement pledge.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have put in place a comprehensive suite of measures to reduce our emissions across all sectors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These measures are complemented by the economy-wide carbon tax which came into effect this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under the Building Control Regulations, all new buildings and buildings undergoing major retrofitting are required to achieve a minimum sustainability standard.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Building and Construction Authority's Green Mark Scheme also encourages building owners and developers to achieve higher energy efficiency, such as by reducing a building's cooling demand and adopting more efficient cooling systems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) has also put in place the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to encourage consumers to purchase more energy-efficient household air-conditioners and introduced the Minimum Energy Performance Standards to phase out the less efficient appliances from the market.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the transport sector, we aim to make public transport the preferred mode of travel in Singapore and to encourage active mobility, such as walking and cycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have already capped the vehicle population in Singapore at zero growth, except for commercial vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also encourage the adoption of cleaner vehicles, including electric vehicles, and are working with the industry to develop infrastructure for our public, shared and private transport vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are diverting waste away from incineration by focusing on efforts to reduce, reuse and recycle.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under the Zero Waste Masterplan launched in August, we outlined how Singapore is adopting a circular economy approach to waste management, where resources are kept in use for as long as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Resource Sustainability Act that was recently enacted gives legislative effect to the regulatory framework that we will put in place to better manage the three priority waste streams of electrical and electronic waste, or e-waste, packaging waste, including plastics, and food waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These measures will contribute not only to reducing carbon emissions and closing the resource loop for these key waste streams but will also extend the lifespan of our only landfill at Semakau.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are closely monitoring global developments in carbon capture and sequestration.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are no plans to incorporate these technologies into our current waste management infrastructure at this moment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, we will continue to study the feasibility of such technology, taking into consideration factors, such as the maturity of the technology, and the costs and benefits of applying it to the Singapore context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Individuals also play a key role in our climate mitigation efforts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We can all choose to make climate-friendly choices and adopt a more sustainable lifestyle, such as setting the air-conditioner temperature at 25°C, practising the 3Rs of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, and taking public transport.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given that air-conditioning that is provided by large-scale district cooling has shown to reduce electricity consumption by more than 30%, are there any plans by the Government to encourage more of such district cooling in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given that it is always a chicken-and-egg problem between having charging points and buying and using electric vehicles, does the Government have any plans to open more public parking spaces for public charging?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Not private charging for the customers of a particular company, but public charging, so as to incentivise more car owners to switch to electric vehicles.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There are presently technologies, such as gasification that does not have harmful emissions and that are compact and modular enough to be deployed locally at our Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Gasification technology can treat food waste and general waste and has shown to be very clean.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does the Government have any plans to introduce such gasification technology in our HDB estates?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are all greenfield sites and it is easier to implement such a technology there.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For brownfield sites, there will be challenges because there are already existing buildings there that have put in place their systems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to electric vehicles, indeed, we encourage the adoption of cleaner energy vehicles, whether it is electric or hybrid, through the Vehicles Emissions Scheme, where we incentivise the purchase of cleaner energy vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards the Member's request for public charging at parking spaces, we will bring his suggestion to the Ministry of Transport and the Land Transport Authority to consider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But in studying this, we will have to take into account factors, such as the overall efficiency of waste treatment at the national level, carbon footprint savings from reduced refuse truck traffic using smaller scale gasification plants, for instance, safety to residents as well as nuisance buffer required for such facilities, especially if we are talking about siting these within HDB estates, and also, any off-take or by-products at the local level.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Just to share that under NEA's regulatory sandbox, the SP Group is conducting a gasification pilot at Gardens by the Bay (GBB).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There, the waste collected from GBB is converted to heat as well as a solid by-product that has got carbon in it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will monitor the outcome of this pilot and assess the feasibility of using such technology for smaller-scale waste treatment facilities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Government looking into battery swapping, as opposed to battery charging, for electric vehicles?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Swapping could potentially be an efficient alternative, given that space is at a premium and so on and so forth?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are studying the infrastructure as well as various measures to encourage the adoption of cleaner energy vehicles, including electric vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is something that we can look into.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that we are only monitoring the technology of carbon capture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask whether the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources is doing a feasibility study of carbon capture as part of our efforts to mitigate climate change?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of the issues, for instance, that we would have to consider is not just economic viability and feasibility, but also whether they meet certain technical requirements, such as environmental standards that have to be met, especially when two-thirds of Singapore is a water catchment area.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are some areas that we will study.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor developments in these technologies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are working with the industry as well as with the research and development sector to look further into the technology.
